memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance to the tent of meeting and wash them with water. Then dress Aaron in the sacred garments, anoint him and consecrate him so he may serve me as priest.'" - Exod 40:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before Aaron could serve, three things happened to him. He was washed. He was clothed. He was anointed.

Notice the order, and notice who acts. Aaron did not wash himself, dress himself, or anoint himself. It was all done to him. He stood there and received.

That is the gospel's order exactly. He saved us through the washing of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit (Titus 3:5). We are clothed with Christ (Gal 3:27). And we have an anointing from the Holy One (1 John 2:20).

Washed, clothed, anointed — then sent to serve.

We get this backwards constantly. We try to serve our way into acceptance, to prove ourselves useful and hope God approves. Scripture reverses it. Acceptance comes first as a gift; service flows from it.

Remember again who Aaron was. The man who had made the golden calf stood at the entrance and was washed clean and dressed in sacred garments. His restoration was not a reward for improvement.

If you feel disqualified today, you are looking at the wrong thing. Stop examining your record and receive what God gives.

Then go and serve.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you serving to earn acceptance or from it?
2. What have you been trying to do for yourself that God wants to do for you?
3. Do you receive God's grace as freely as He offers it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, wash me, clothe me and set me apart. I cannot do any of it for myself. Amen.
